McKenzie Farms in Fairhope, Alabama has opened its corn maze for a second season, but this year the attraction carries deeper meaning as a tribute to a farmer who died in an accident, according to WKRG News 5.

The seasonal fall tradition draws families to navigate the intricate paths cut through the cornfield, offering a popular weekend activity for the area. While the maze itself returns as an annual fixture, organizers have incorporated the remembrance into this year's experience.

The farm has become a gathering spot for the community during the fall season, combining the appeal of a classic harvest-time activity with a meaningful acknowledgment of loss. Details about the specific accident and the farmer being honored were not immediately available.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Destin has approved paid parking at Norriego Point, a popular beach access point on Gulf Shore Drive, according to a city council decision announced on social media. Visitors will now pay $5 per hour to park at the location.

The move comes as the city seeks to manage parking demand at one of its beach parks. Norriego Point serves as a public access point to the Gulf and has been a draw for both locals and tourists visiting the Destin area.

The decision reflects a growing trend among coastal Florida municipalities to implement or adjust parking fees at high-traffic beach and park locations to help fund maintenance and manage vehicle congestion during peak seasons.

item.content:encoded:
A firefighter in Bay Minette, Alabama is being recognized this month for going above and beyond while helping a woman who experienced multiple falls. Christian Hall with the Bay Minette Fire Department received September's "Smiles Behind the Shield" award from WKRG News 5, an honor that celebrated his compassionate approach to emergency response.

According to WKRG, Hall's recognition came as a surprise when the news station showed up at his fire station with his family present to deliver the award. The gesture highlighted the kind of personal touch and genuine care that Hall brings to his work as a first responder in the community.

The "Smiles Behind the Shield" program recognizes first responders across the region who demonstrate exceptional compassion and commitment beyond their typical duties. Hall's selection underscores the importance of the emotional and human side of emergency services, not just the technical response.

item.content:encoded:
Two people died Thursday after their vehicle was struck by an Amtrak train near Theodore, authorities say. According to WKRG News 5, the crash happened at a railroad crossing near Bellingrath Road and Peary Road after the vehicle attempted to bypass the crossing gates.

Police say the driver tried to beat the train across the tracks, resulting in the collision. The incident marks a tragic reminder of the dangers of ignoring railroad crossing safety warnings.

The names and additional circumstances surrounding the crash have not yet been released. The investigation is ongoing.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

The commenter's uncertainty about what happened to the polluted material and why the site…
item.content:encoded:
A social media conversation this week highlights how little many Pensacola residents may know about the area's industrial environmental past — specifically a Superfund cleanup site tied to polychlorinated biphenyls, or PCBs, that once contaminated local soil.

The commenter's uncertainty about what happened to the polluted material and why the site warranted federal Superfund designation reflects a broader knowledge gap in the community about one of Pensacola's most significant environmental remediation efforts. The Superfund program, established in the 1980s, targets the nation's most contaminated properties for cleanup.

While local authorities did take the cleanup seriously, the specifics of soil removal, testing protocols, and final disposition of hazardous material remain unfamiliar to many longtime Pensacola residents who lived through the remediation process. Environmental cleanup records are generally public, though they require effort to locate through EPA databases and local environmental agencies.

item.title: UWF President Diaz Among DeSantis Associates Now Leading Florida Universities
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: University of West Florida President Manny Diaz Jr. is among a growing roster of DeSantis political allies and former staffers who have taken the helm of Florida's public universities and colleges, according to a social media post tracking the appointments. Diaz joins six other DeSantis-connected figures now serving as university presidents across…
item.content:encoded:
University of West Florida President Manny Diaz Jr. is among a growing roster of DeSantis political allies and former staffers who have taken the helm of Florida's public universities and colleges, according to a social media post tracking the appointments.

Diaz joins six other DeSantis-connected figures now serving as university presidents across the state, including Jeanette Nuñez at Florida International University, Richard Corcoran at New College of Florida, Marva Johnson at Florida A&M University, Adam Hasner at Florida Atlantic University, Alex Kelly at Pensacola State College, and Anastasios "Stasi" Kamoutsas at Polk State College.

The pattern reflects the governor's influence over higher education leadership in Florida. UWF appointed Diaz to its presidency in 2023, positioning him to oversee the Pensacola-area university as it navigates state education policy under the DeSantis administration. His tenure comes as Florida's higher education system faces significant policy shifts, including controversial curriculum and governance changes at state universities.

While the specific species and weights weren't detailed in the initial release, the accomplishments highlight the rich fishing opportunities available along the Mississippi Gulf Coast. The records come as fall fishing season brings optimal conditions for saltwater anglers throughout the region.

Fishermen in the broader Gulf area, including those based in Northwest Florida, often compete for similar records and frequently travel between Mississippi and Florida waters for prime fishing seasons. For anyone interested in pursuing their own records, both Mississippi and Florida maintain official record-keeping systems for saltwater catches.

item.content:encoded:
Probate disagreements often stem from three core issues: confusion over who should manage an estate, disputes about how assets get divided, and conflicting interpretations of what a deceased person actually wanted, according to Pensacola-based Boyles and Boyles, PLLC.

The local law firm says the most common flashpoints in estate administration center on unclear instructions left behind and family members disagreeing over roles and responsibilities during the probate process.

To help families navigate these sensitive matters, the firm is offering a conflict-reduction guide designed to clarify estate administration and reduce friction among heirs. Those interested can reach out to attorney Joseph Boyles at 850.433.9225 or visit boylesandboyleslaw.com for more information.

item.title: Sen. Scott Introduces Bill to Block Foreign Child Predators from US Visas
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled legislation Thursday aimed at strengthening vetting procedures for foreign visa applicants by giving federal agencies access to child exploitation databases. The SCREEN Act — Strengthened Checks for Reliable Evaluation of Entrants Nationwide — would allow the Department of Homeland Security and State Department to…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled legislation Thursday aimed at strengthening vetting procedures for foreign visa applicants by giving federal agencies access to child exploitation databases.

The SCREEN Act — Strengthened Checks for Reliable Evaluation of Entrants Nationwide — would allow the Department of Homeland Security and State Department to access records from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children during visa processing. Currently, that data is shared only with certain law enforcement agencies, a gap Scott says has allowed foreign workers with child sexual abuse material to slip through.

The bill was prompted by recent reports that cruise lines and other employers hired foreign workers on temporary C-1/D visas who were later found with child sexual abuse material. Scott called the current system a bureaucratic failure. "The greatest country in the history of the world should have 100% certainty that we aren't letting child predators come here on work visas," Scott said in a statement.

Representative Carlos Giménez introduced companion legislation in the House, with Senator Ted Budd as an original cosponsor. The lawmakers say interagency coordination is essential to both national security and protecting American children from exploitation.
